summary: Concrete light and fog signal at the entrance to Prince William Sound, built 1909-10 after the steamer Oregon grounded and rebuilt in 1934 as the first of Alaska's Art Deco lighthouses.

access.note: Coast Guard property; grounds and tower closed; best seen by boat or plane from Cordova.

notes_for_editor: Roster: only the first few keepers are listed in the research JSON; the full roster comes from the USLHS archive. Lighthouse Friends and the archive disagree on Shoemaker's 1922-1929 service and on Lee Harpole dates (not used). Oregon 1906 passenger count differs (about 50 vs 126). Armeria rescue: NRHP says keepers rescued the crew; Valdez Daily Prospector and Lighthouse Friends say the steamer Sampson. 1923 vs 1922 diaphone date noted. The Tinkham anecdote is undated and second-hand via Lighthouse Friends. Dimensions of the 1934 building differ between NRHP and Lighthouse Friends and were left out. Nomination page numbers are the form's printed page numbers. Lens replacement: Lighthouse Friends says 1967 aerobeacon, NRHP says original lens used until 1971 (DCB-224); the story states both. NRHP also mentions a '1971 automation program' against its own 'automated in 1974'. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Oregon passenger count 'fifty' per Lighthouse Friends.
